svg.title: Fig. 125 — A rectangular hyperbola inverted at a vertex: the strophoid
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 125, page 129. Section: inversion.

g.data-text: The circle of inversion about the vertex O (radius 2a) and the rectangular hyperbola (x + a)² − y² = a², with its asymptotes.
Take a point P of the hyperbola and find its inverse P̄ on the ray OP. The vertex (−2a, 0) lies on the circle of inversion and so is its own inverse.
The inverse: the ordinary strophoid. The branch through O goes to the two arms (asymptote x = 2a), the other branch to the loop; the asymptotes of the hyperbola become the tangents of the node at O.
